If the returned records include stable identifiers or shared attributes (e.g., email, username, internal user ID) beyond what is strictly necessary for authentication, the process can link a person's activity or account across sessions, services, or contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the users collection contains persistent identifiers and /api/auth accesses or propagates them during authentication.
uncertainty_note: Threat depends on the specific fields read and whether identifiers are exposed or reused outside strict authentication logic.

title: Authentication process may access excessive user attributes
description: When /api/auth reads from the users collection, it may retrieve more personal data than needed for login, such as profile fields, metadata, or historical information. This creates a risk of identifying individuals more precisely than necessary and increases privacy exposure within the authentication process.
assumptions: Assumes database queries are not data-minimized and may fetch whole user documents rather than only credentials/required account state.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is based on best judgment because the exact threat-tree mapping for identifyability at a DataStore->Process read was not provided in the retrieved context.

title: Reading users collection may disclose personal data to the authentication process beyond necessity
description: The data flow transfers user data from the MongoDB users collection to /api/auth. If the flow includes unnecessary personal data, sensitive fields, or full user documents, personal information becomes disclosed within the process scope without a need-to-know basis, increasing the chance of misuse, logging exposure, or later leakage.
assumptions: Assumes user documents contain personal data beyond minimal authentication material and that /api/auth can access those fields.

title: Authentication reads may expose that a person has an account
description: A read from the users collection by /api/auth can reveal whether a specific individual exists in the system. If the process behavior, outputs, timing, or errors differ depending on whether a matching user record is found, an attacker or unauthorized party could detect the presence of a user's account or infer participation in the service.
assumptions: Assumes externally observable differences in /api/auth behavior when records are found versus absent.

title: Authentication may process user records without a valid legal basis or compatible purpose
description: The /api/auth process reads personal data from the users collection for authentication. If the collection also contains attributes collected for other purposes, or if retention and use are not properly constrained, this flow may process data without valid consent, contract necessity, or another appropriate legal basis, or in a way incompatible with the original purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the users collection may contain mixed-purpose personal data and governance controls may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on organizational/legal context not visible in the DFD alone; included because purpose limitation and lawful-basis issues are a common privacy risk for authentication data access.

title: Users may be unaware that authentication reads broader account data
description: Data subjects may not be adequately informed that logging in causes /api/auth to read personal data from the users collection, potentially including metadata or account attributes beyond credentials. Lack of transparency about this read and its scope can undermine awareness and the user's ability to understand privacy impact.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices or in-product explanations do not clearly describe the scope of data accessed during authentication.
uncertainty_note: This threat is grounded in transparency/unawareness rather than the technical read alone, so applicability depends on the surrounding notice and UX.

title: User records written to the users collection may be linkable across contexts
description: The /api/auth process writes user account data into a central MongoDB users collection. If identifiers such as email address, username, device/account identifiers, or stable internal user IDs are stored together, records from authentication, profile management, and later application activity can be linked to the same individual across contexts, enabling profiling beyond what is necessary for authentication.
assumptions: Assumes the users collection stores persistent identifiers and/or attributes that are reused by other processes or features.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selection is best-effort based on common LINDDUN Pro linkability decomposition; exact node id may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Stored authentication-related user data may enable identification of individuals
description: Writing users into the MongoDB users collection can place directly identifying or quasi-identifying data at rest, such as names, email addresses, phone numbers, usernames, or combined account metadata. This can make data subjects identifiable from the stored records, especially if the datastore is queried or combined with other application data.
assumptions: Assumes the written user records contain direct identifiers or sufficiently unique account attributes.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is inferred from standard identifiability-at-rest threats; specific subnode naming may differ across LINDDUN Pro releases.

title: Users may be unable to prove or contest what account data was written
description: If /api/auth writes user records without privacy-relevant auditability, data subjects may later be unable to demonstrate what personal data was submitted, whether consent- or preference-related fields were captured correctly, or whether an account record was created/updated legitimately. This weakens accountability around privacy-relevant processing.
assumptions: Assumes creation/update events and key data-field provenance are not logged in a privacy-preserving, reviewable way.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation in LINDDUN is often interpreted as lack of plausible deniability/accountability support; applicability depends on whether provenance and review needs are in scope for this auth write flow.

title: Sensitive account attributes in the users collection may be disclosed
description: The auth process writes user data into a persistent datastore. If the record includes credentials, password hashes, recovery information, security questions, contact details, tokens, or profile attributes, unauthorized access to the collection or overbroad internal access could disclose personal data and authentication-related secrets.
assumptions: Assumes the users collection contains personal data and possibly authentication-related fields beyond a minimal opaque identifier.
uncertainty_note: Generic disclosure-at-rest threat clearly applies, but exact subnode id is an informed approximation.

title: The users collection may contain more personal data than necessary for authentication
description: A write flow from /api/auth to the users collection can encourage central accumulation of account, profile, device, recovery, and behavioral metadata. If fields not strictly required for authentication or account lifecycle are stored, the datastore enables excessive granularity and retention of personal data, increasing privacy impact.
assumptions: Assumes schema design may include optional or convenience fields beyond strict authentication needs.
uncertainty_note: This is a standard data minimization threat for a write-to-datastore flow; exact node id may differ in your LINDDUN Pro taxonomy.

This creates a transparency and intervenability gap around the write operation.
assumptions: Assumes the interface or privacy notice does not clearly explain the fields stored and their purposes/retention.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is inferred from the flow alone; confirmation would require UX/notice and control details.

Storing extra fields or reusing auth-collected data for secondary purposes can create non-compliance with privacy principles such as purpose limitation, data minimization, and lawful basis.

uncertainty_note: Compliance threats depend heavily on jurisdiction, notice, lawful basis, and actual schema/purpose; inclusion is justified as a plausible privacy threat for this write flow but needs validation.
